title: Seahawks Add Joe Mixon to Banged-Up Backfield
htmlContent:
The Seattle Seahawksare leaning on experience to patch a backfield that has been hit hard over the past few weeks. Veteran running back Joe Mixon worked out for the team Monday morning and is expected to sign, head coach Mike Macdonald said, with the two-time Pro Bowler set to begin his Seattle tenure on the practice squad.

"We're down runners," Macdonald said. "We need running backs. He's a good running back."

Mixon, 30, sat out all of the 2025 season with a foot injury. The last time he carried a full workload, in 2024 with the Houston Texans, he piled up 1,016 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns.

A Backfield Running Low on Bodies

Seattle is currently without its two most talented running backs. Rookie Jadarian Price landed on injured reserve Saturday with a chest and shoulder injury and will be sidelined for at least three more games.

Zach Charbonnet, who paced the Seahawks with 12 rushing touchdowns in 2025, opened this season on the physically unable to perform list while recovering from an ACL tear suffered in January. He has not appeared in a game yet. He returned to practice Thursday, opening a 21-day activation window, but still needs to regain game shape and is not expected to play this week against the San Francisco 49ers.

Seattle also let former lead back Kenneth Walker leave for the Kansas City Chiefs in free agency this offseason.

Wilson Carries the Load Against the Chargers

Without Price or Charbonnet, the Seahawks still ran for 138 yards in Sunday's 30-23 win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Reserve Emanuel Wilsonhandled the bulk of the work, gaining 81 yards on 21 carries while hauling in three passes for 39 yards. He found the end zone twice. George Holani added 18 yards on seven attempts, and wide receiver and return specialist Rashid Shaheedbroke loose for a 28-yard touchdown run after lining up in the backfield behind quarterback Sam Darnold.

Four games into the season, Seattle sits 13th in the league at 110.3 rushing yards per game and has topped 100 yards twice.

Mixon Celebrates His Return

"12's WHAT'S HATNIN!!!!!" Mixon posted on X on October 5.

In a separate post, he reflected on the road that brought him back.

"Y'all just don't know, what I been through this passed year & a half… Just know that's all God," Mixon wrote. "He will test your faith, keep trusting, stay patient, and believe in His timing. Never lose hope or give up. Your breakthrough is coming."

The Schultz Report's Jordan Schultz was among the first to report the move.

"Sources: The #Seahawks are signing 2x RB Joe Mixon," Schultz wrote on X, describing it as "a return to the NFL for the talented RB with rookie Jadarian Price on IR, as Mixon will wear No. 25."

Schultz followed up with details on what sealed the deal.

"Seattle wanted to make sure Joe Mixon was in shape, so they brought him in and were very impressed with the type of condition he kept himself in," he wrote. "It's my understanding that Mixon will start on PS."

Practice Squad First, Then a Path to the Field

Macdonald later confirmed the practice squad plan during his day-after media session. Under league rules, Seattle can elevate Mixon to the game-day roster three times. After that, the team would have to sign him to the 53-man roster or move in another direction.

A Proven Track Record in Cincinnati and Houston

The Cincinnati Bengals drafted Mixon in the second round, 48th overall, in 2017. After seven seasons as a dual-threat back in Cincinnati, he was traded to Houston before 2024 and delivered right away.

Things shifted quickly after that. Mixon has not played since Houston's loss in the AFC Divisional Playoffs following the 2024 season. The Texans shared few details about his injury, and the team released him in March at his request. Away from the field, Mixon has launched an athletic apparel company called OneSock.

His career body of work remains impressive. Across eight seasons, Mixon has rushed 1,816 times for 7,428 yards and 60 touchdowns, and caught 319 passes for 2,448 yards and 14 more scores. He earned Pro Bowl nods in 2021 and 2024 and was named to the NFL's Top 100 Players list in 2022 and 2025. He has made $55.4 million over his career.

Motivation on Both Sides

Mixon's journey has taken him from a Bengals team that reached the Super Bowl, to a contending Texans club, and now to the reigning champion Seahawks. The specifics of what wiped out his 2025 season may never be made public.

What is clear is that the fit makes sense for everyone involved. Seattle needs an experienced runner until its top backs return, and Mixon gets a chance to prove he can still produce on a contender.
excerpt: The Seattle Seahawks are signing veteran running back Joe Mixon to the practice squad after a workout Monday, with head coach Mike Macdonald confirming the move as Seattle deals with injuries to Jadarian Price and Zach Charbonnet and the offseason departure of Kenneth Walker.
